title: Your first investigation
summary: Someone changed the school Wi-Fi welcome page using a teacher's account. Learn ls, cat, head, tail, grep, wc, cut, sort, uniq and sha256sum one at a time, and find the password guessing attack behind it.
ctf: A flag is hidden in the Wi-Fi banner the attacker changed (step 11). Submit it on the CTF board as "Your first investigation".

title: The invoice that wasn't
summary: A fake overdue invoice reaches three people at Kestrel Logistics. One opens it. An hour later the HR and Finance folders are encrypted. Find patient zero, trace the attack, contain it and choose a backup to restore.
ctf: The loader's campaign value hides a flag (step 7). Submit it on the CTF board as "The invoice that wasn't".

title: The night shift download
summary: An engineer who has just resigned to join a competitor badges into an empty office at 01:47. Build a timeline from badge, VPN, Git, USB and DLP records, and handle it the right way: evidence first, then HR and Legal.
ctf: The USB drive's volume label is a flag (step 6). Submit it on the CTF board as "The night shift download".

title: Exam day outage
summary: Five minutes into an online exam, the school's portal stops answering, and an extortion email arrives. Tell real students from attack traffic, name the three kinds of flood, and choose how to get the exam back.
ctf: The HTTP flood's user agent carries a flag (step 4). Submit it on the CTF board as "Exam day outage".

title: The hacked web shop
summary: NimbuMart's web server is busy and sending data out. Follow the attacker from SQL injection to a web shell, a hidden backdoor and a command server.
ctf: The attacker signed their notes with a crew tag (step 7). Submit it on the CTF board as "Follow the beacon home".

title: The key in the commit
summary: A deploy key with admin rights sat in an old Git commit. The repo went public for one evening. By 02:00 someone had copied customer data, made a backdoor admin and started 20 crypto-miners. Trace it, shut it down and fix the root cause.
ctf: A flag sits in the deleted config file's Git history (step 3). Submit it on the CTF board as "The key in the commit".

title: The miner in the build server
summary: Brightloom Games' build server has run at full CPU all night. Trace a brute-forced CI login to a script console, a dropper, three kinds of persistence and a cryptominer talking to a mining pool, then clean up and rebuild.
ctf: One of the attacker's ways back in carries a flag in its comment (step 7). Submit it on the CTF board as "The miner in the build server".

title: Quiet DNS
summary: A Finance laptop at Harbourline Credit Union never touched the internet, yet a confidential file left the building. Find the DNS tunnel, measure it, and rebuild the stolen file from base32 chunks hidden in query names.
ctf: The stolen file's doc-id is a flag, once you rebuild it from the DNS chunks (step 7). Submit it on the CTF board as "Quiet DNS".

title: Who changed the grades?
kicker: Teacher case: insider and access control
summary: Grades changed under a teacher's name, in subjects he doesn't teach, from a student lab PC. Use the audit log, sign-in records and lab logins to find out how, and fix the access control.
ctf: One changed grade has a base64 comment. Decode it for the flag (step 4). Submit it on the CTF board.

title: Password spraying at the library portal
summary: Nobody was locked out, yet a library member's account was taken over. Find the slow password spray, the one account it opened and what the attacker changed.
ctf: The attacker renamed the account they took over. That new name is the flag (step 4). Submit it on the CTF board.

title: The QR code parking fine
summary: Fake parking fines arrive by text and by QR stickers on parking meters. Compare the fake site with the real one and find where the card details go.
ctf: The phishing kit left a build comment in its page (step 4). That is the flag. Submit it on the CTF board.
